{{Quote|The ultimate in modern reconnaissance techniques&mdash;one of the wartime technologies developed by Dr. Godera, praise his crazed heart.|Theron Shan|<ref name="Lost 3" />}}
A '''spy ray''' was a sophisticated surveillance device developed by [[Doctor/Legends|Doctor]] [[Nasan Godera]] for the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] during the [[Great Galactic War]] with the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Sith Empire]]. By projecting beams of particles that would pass through or reflect off of matter depending on the object's density, the [[Spy/Legends|spy]] ray was able to generate high-resolution images of targets across an entire [[Star system/Legends|star system]], and it saw great use in the hands of the [[Republic Strategic Information Service|Strategic Information Service]], the Republic's primary intelligence agency.

==Characteristics==
{{Quote|The spy ray projects a beam of particles that pass through or reflect off matter, depending on the beam's intensity.|Theron Shan|<ref name="Lost 3" />}}
The [[Spy/Legends|spy]] ray was built with a square base that supported a long, rectangular section that could pivot and rotate to focus on the target. It was controlled by a panel on the side of the base, which allowed the user to adjust the settings and view the ray's target through an apparatus similar in shape to [[Electrobinoculars/Legends|electrobinoculars]]. When activated, the spy ray projected a beam of particles that would either reflect off the target or pass through it, depending on the intensity of the beam. The particles that were reflected would be translated into high-resolution images of the target by the spy ray's base, allowing the user to view objects as small as the [[Mouth/Legends|mouth]] of a [[Shyrack/Legends|shyrack]] across an entire [[Star system/Legends|star system]].<ref name="Lost 3" /> While it was not designed as a weapon, the spy ray's beam could be adjusted to bring its frequency with ranges that weaponized it. Additionally, the spy ray had a minimum safe distance of 500 [[Kilometer/Legends|kilometers]], as objects subjected to the beam at a distance less than were likely to disintegrate.<ref name="Encyclopedia" /> The materials necessary to build a spy ray were enough for three [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoids]] and an [[Astromech droid/Legends|astromech droid]] to carry in large [[Backpack/Legends|backpacks]], though it took at least two [[Standard day/Legends|days]] for three people to build one.<ref name="Lost 3" />

==History==
[[File:Spy_ray_building.jpg|thumb|right|140px|A spy ray under construction]]
{{Quote|In two days, our orbit will give us a clear view of the inner planets. If Darth Mekhis built anything, that's where we need to look. We've got the best spy rays and telescopes the S.I.S. can provide. Let's get to work.|Theron Shan|<ref name="Lost 3" />}}
The spy ray was originally created by [[Doctor/Legends|Doctor]] [[Nasan Godera]],<ref name="Lost 3" /> a [[Scientist/Legends|scientist]] who served as the [[Engineer/Legends|chief designer]] for the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic's]] [[Advanced Development Laboratories]] during the [[Great Galactic War]] with the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Sith Empire]]. Godera finished the device sometime before the end of the war in [[3653 BBY]], when he resigned in disgust over the Republic's acceptance of the [[Treaty of Coruscant]].<ref name="Encyclopedia" /> The spy ray was considered to be the best reconnaissance technology of its [[Time/Legends|time]] during the subsequent [[Cold War (Galactic Republic–Sith Empire)|Cold War]], where it saw use by the Republic's intelligence agency, the [[Republic Strategic Information Service]]. SIS [[Agent/Legends|agent]] [[Theron Shan]] was trained in the construction of the spy ray, and he kept the necessary materials aboard his [[Starship/Legends|ship]],<ref name="Lost 3" /> the ''[[Sojourner]]'',<ref name="Annihilation">''[[The Old Republic: Annihilation]]''</ref> in case he needed to use it.<ref name="Lost 3" />

On a [[Mission to the Vesla system|mission]] to the Imperial-held [[Vesla system/Legends|Vesla system]] to investigate what the [[Dark Council]]or [[Darth Mekhis]] was doing there, Shan constructed a spy ray on an [[Unidentified planetoid (Vesla system)|outlying planet]] with the help of the [[Twi'lek/Legends|Twi'lek]] [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggler]] [[Teff'ith]]; the [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Ngani Zho]]; and his astromech, [[M-6]]. After two days of construction, Shan used it to examine the [[Planet/Legends|planets]] [[Vesla Two]] and [[Vesla Three]]&mdash;only to find that Mekhis had tested [[Superweapon/Legends|superweapons]] against the worlds, and that the Imperials were using a [[Space station/Legends|space station]] known as the [[Sun Razer]] to harvest the energy of the system's [[Star/Legends|sun]] and construct superweapons. However, the spy ray was left behind when Shan realized the Empire was capable of seeing through the scanner interference caused by the Sun Razer, and the trio was captured aboard the ''Sojourner'' by the [[Harrower-class dreadnought|''Harrower''-class dreadnought]] ''[[Valor Prevails]]'' as they tried to leave the planet's [[Atmosphere/Legends|atmosphere]].<ref name="Lost 3" />

==Behind the scenes==
The spy ray first appeared in [[The Old Republic — The Lost Suns 3|Part 3]] of [[Star Wars: The Old Republic — The Lost Suns|''The Lost Suns'']], a story arc in the [[Star Wars: The Old Republic (comic series)|''Star Wars: The Old Republic'' comic series]], published in [[August]] [[2011]]. In keeping with the rest of the arc, which introduced a number of characters and locations that would later appear in the [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]'', the issue used the spy ray to introduce Doctor Nasan Godera, the weapon's designer and a character who would play a major role in the game's [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] and [[Imperial Agent]] class storylines.<ref name="Lost 3" /> A reference guide for the game released in [[2012]], ''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic Encyclopedia]]'', included the spy ray in a list of Doctor Godera's projects in the entry on him.<ref name="Encyclopedia" />
